issue: Author is matched with case-sensitive `instr(author, ?)` instead of `LIKE ? ESCAPE '\'`, so author searches break AC2 and AC3, and author and title are matched inconsistently.
evidence: q=fowler: instr('Martin Fowler','fowler') = 0 and title 'Refactoring' has no 'fowler', so the AC2 example returns [] instead of including Refactoring. q=Fowler matches, so case changes the result.

issue: `_` is not escaped before the LIKE, so it acts as a single-character wildcard on title. This breaks AC8.
evidence: q=_ gives pattern '%_%', which matches every non-empty title, so all 50 seed books come back instead of []. q=c_ean also matches 'Clean Code'.

issue: Off-by-one in the length check: `>=` rejects a trimmed query of exactly 100 characters. AC6 requires 200 at 100 characters and 400 only at 101 or more.
evidence: With MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 100, q='a'.repeat(100) makes q.length >= 100 true, so the request returns 400 instead of 200. The check should be `>`.

issue: q is not checked to be a single string. String() coerces arrays and objects instead of returning 400 { error: 'Query must be a single string' }.
evidence: ?q=a&q=b gives req.query.q = ['a','b'], which String() turns into 'a,b' and returns 200 []. ?q[x]=1 becomes '[object Object]'. The required error message does not appear anywhere in the code.
